text:
raj_support: @sam_sre fyi ACME (maria) opened a ticket — they've been seeing repeated 502s and p95 spikes on hosted inference since 2026-03-17T09:10Z. They included request-id 01FZ9X7A and example headers.

sam_sre: Looking at gateway metrics for us-west1 now. pulling logs...

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-4799991111 — suspected gateway 502s affecting text-generation endpoints.

jordan_eng: Any common denominator? model family? embeddings vs generate?

raj_support: Only text-generation endpoints. Customer says the spikes coincide with a background ingestion job that bursts concurrent requests. They reported SDK retries didn't help and mentioned duplicate billing hits.

sam_sre: Confirmed: gateway 502 count increased from ~09:09–09:25 UTC in us-west1. Upstream runtime returning 502s and we see elevated write latencies to billing-collector service. Correlation looks strong.

elaine_support: Customer asked for immediate mitigation. Suggested they throttle client side: set SDK max_concurrency=4 and exponential backoff with jitter.

jordan_eng: Attempting local repro with a small hammer test. Script used:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"test"}' &
done
wait
```
Observed ~6% 502s and p95 ~2.8s under burst.

sam_sre: Gateway and runtime traces show billing-collector calls timing out around ~1.2–1.6s which causes the runtime to return 502 instead of queuing. Billing-collector logs show Dynamo throttling on a hot partition.

jordan_eng: Quick workaround: introduce local async buffer for billing events and drain in batches, or short-circuit sync billing path behind a feature flag `billing.async_buffer=true` so requests don't block on billing writes. I'll draft a PR.

raj_support: Drafting customer update to ACME:
"We're actively investigating the 5xxs on hosted inference. Early signs point to a billing subsystem call that's timing out under bursty traffic; we're deploying a temporary feature flag to queue billing writes asynchronously to prevent request-level failures. Recommend pausing the burst job or reducing concurrency to 4 while we roll this change. No data loss expected; we'll follow up with ETA"

maria_acme: Thanks. We can pause the job if you need us to. We're worried about being billed for failed attempts though — any way to avoid double charges?

elaine_support: We will suppress billing for requests that ultimately failed due to gateway 5xxs during the incident window. We'll track request-ids and reconcile. ETA for canary is ~2 hours.

incident-bot: Deploy started: canary `billing-buffer=true` to us-west1 (deploy-789).

sam_sre: Early canary metrics look good — 502 rate in canary drops from ~6% to 0.5%, p95 down to ~420ms. Keeping an eye on billing backlog metrics.

jordan_eng: PR: https://git.internal/rwd/infra/pulls/333 — adds flag + metrics (queued_count, drain_latency). Will add a kill-switch if backlog grows.

raj_support: Customer notified and asked to hold their job. Follow-ups: billing ops to investigate Dynamo partitioning and long-term mitigation. Ops owners: @jordan_eng, @sam_sre.

maria_acme: Appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll stay paused and confirm once you give the all-clear.

elaine_support: Marking for postmortem if billing ops confirm infra-level partitioning issue. Will update internal incident doc with timeline and billing reconciliation plan. :thumbsup:
